source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: In the pipeline diagram described in the lecture, what does the ellipsis ('...') between two decoder stacks represent?

options.text: A pause where the model stops to check its work before continuing.
options.feedback: That describes something closer to reasoning or looping, both of which are separate ideas. The ellipsis is a drawing convention, not a step the model takes.

options.text: A missing part of the diagram that was never finished.
options.feedback: The ellipsis is deliberate, not an unfinished drawing. It stands for content that is real but too repetitive to draw out.

options.text: A stand-in for however many more decoder stacks the model actually has.
options.feedback: Only two stacks fit on the slide, but a real pipeline repeats the same attention-then-MLP (multi-layer perceptron) pattern many more times than a diagram can show.

options.text: The point where image tokens are converted into word tokens.
options.feedback: No conversion between token types happens there. The ellipsis marks more repetitions of the same decoder stack pattern.
